summary: “A Sojourner Tale” is an interactive story created by the team Cosmic Crew Girls for the NASA Space Apps challenge “Abandoned but not Forgotten.” Inspired by the Mars Pathfinder mission, it is narrated in the first person by the Sojourner rover across eight animated chapters, covering its launch in 1996, airbag landing, first steps, rock encounters, solar-powered days, and a mission that lasted 83 sols instead of the planned 7. Users can tap five glowing hotspots to explore the rover’s parts, open cards of real NASA data (such as 2.3 billion bits returned and 16,500+ lander images), and turn on read-aloud narration. Designed for young learners, it works on phones and computers and ends by honoring Sojourner’s legacy, which leads to Perseverance. It is built with HTML, CSS, SVG and JavaScript.
details:
A Sojourner Tale: An Interactive Digital Story Inspired by NASA's Mars Pathfinder Mission

A Sojourner Tale is an interactive storytelling website based on NASA's Mars Pathfinder mission and its small rover, Sojourner. Sojourner tells the story itself, in the first person, so visitors follow the trip from Earth to Mars through the rover's eyes. I didn't want the site to be another list of dates and facts. It mixes storytelling with science, illustrations, animations and interactive features to make space exploration feel more alive and easier to follow.

The story moves through the main stages of the mission. It starts with the launch from Earth, then goes through the landing on Mars, the rover's first movements, its study of rocks and soil, what it discovered, and how it shaped later Mars missions. Mars Pathfinder launched on December 4, 1996, and landed in Ares Vallis on July 4, 1997. The site explains the airbag system that cushioned the landing and introduces some of the rocks Sojourner studied, including Barnacle Bill, Yogi and Scooby-Doo. Visitors also learn about the rover itself: it weighed only about 10.6 kg, stood around 30 cm tall and moved on six wheels.

The project runs in any web browser. Visitors scroll through the story chapter by chapter. They can also click hotspots on the rover illustration to explore its parts: the solar panel, cameras, APXS instrument, wheels and body. Information cards and pop-ups give extra details about the mission, the instruments and the discoveries. Animated backgrounds, smooth transitions, a scroll progress bar and a read-aloud option make the site more engaging and more accessible.

I built the website with HTML, CSS and JavaScript:

  1. HTML gives the site its structure and splits the story into sections.
  2. CSS handles the layout, colours, animations, transitions and responsive design.
  3. JavaScript runs the interactive parts, including chapter navigation, hotspots, pop-ups, scroll tracking and the animated backgrounds.
  4. SVG illustrations draw the rover and the Martian landscape.
  5. The Canvas API creates the moving star background.
  6. The browser's Web Speech API provides the read-aloud narration.

Together, these let the site work without special hardware or any software to install.

One of the project's biggest strengths is how it makes scientific and historical information simple to take in. Space missions, scientific instruments and planetary exploration can feel overwhelming, but they become much easier to understand when they're told as a story with visuals you can interact with. The site can be useful for school and college students, teachers, and anyone curious about space. Because the design is responsive, it works on computers, tablets and phones.

The main goal of A Sojourner Tale is to spark interest in planetary exploration. It shows how a rover weighing only about 10.6 kg made a big difference to our understanding of Mars. It also tested technologies that later missions built on. By combining real science with a story, I hope the project encourages people, especially students, to get curious about science, technology, engineering and space.

The creative side of the project comes from telling the mission from Sojourner's point of view. Instead of treating it as just a machine, the website gives the rover a voice, so visitors feel like they're travelling with it. Space-themed visuals, Martian scenery, interactive illustrations, animations and narration make the mission more memorable. The story also links Sojourner's work to the rovers that followed it: Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity and Perseverance.

While building the site, I focused on keeping the science accurate, ordering the story so it made sense, making the interactions smooth and keeping it easy to navigate on any device. No physical rover or electronic hardware is needed; a browser is enough. In the future, I'd like to add more detailed animations, interactive maps, quizzes, more information about the scientific instruments, and narration in other languages.

In short, A Sojourner Tale brings together technology, creativity, education and storytelling to share what the Mars Pathfinder mission achieved. A rover small enough to carry in your arms helped change how we explore space, which shows that even a small step on another planet can help us understand the universe.
